content.name: Invitation response record
content.description: Represent an explicitly supplied invitation and reply as component-level stance, permission and proposed next-step data.

inputs.invitation: Exact text and separately named requested components.
inputs.reply: Exact supplied text; absent reply is allowed and remains unknown.
inputs.actor_scope: Constructed or actual, known speaker and relevant role.
inputs.context: Only explicit timing, access and prior permission supplied with the case.

outputs.response_record: For each requested component: evidence span, accepted/declined/conditional/unknown stance, stated condition, next-step proposal and confirmation status.
outputs.unknowns: Missing meanings that would change stance or next step.

success_criteria: Every component has a stance or explicit unknown.
Accepted scope does not exceed the evidence span.
A proposed change remains a proposal until a reply accepts it.
steps: Keep the invitation components and exact reply text together.
Associate each explicit reply clause with its requested component.
Record accepted, declined, conditional or unknown stance for each component; retain stated conditions.
Separate the speaker's stated reason from a hypothesis about motive.
Create a next-step proposal only for an unresolved component that matters to the invitation.
Return the evidence-bearing response record and unresolved meanings.
verification: Trace each non-unknown stance to the supplied text.
Compare the scope of every accepted component with its evidence.
Check that proposed action is not recorded as recipient agreement.
content.complexity: moderate: semantic clause-to-component mapping requires judgment.
dependencies: Existing explicit goal and invitation components; original AL offers paraphrase preparation but cannot supply an absent reply.
content.reuse_potential: Local analysis of exploratory invitations, workshop roles and bounded help requests.
when_to_use: A concrete invitation has separable requests and a supplied reply or explicit absence of reply.
Preparing a bounded collaboration draft without claiming live confirmation.

examples.input: Invitation: read and host. Reply: I will read two pages; I cannot host.
examples.output: Reading accepted for two pages; hosting declined; no motive inferred.

examples.input: Invitation: join once. Reply: Only if it is audio.
examples.output: Joining conditional on audio; a proposed audio arrangement remains unconfirmed.
Attendance stance unknown; no assent or disinterest inferred.

examples.input: Invitation: read. Reply: I like the idea but cannot take this on.
examples.output: Positive stated interest; task declined; the predicates coexist.

failure_modes.consequence: A bounded acceptance spreads to another request.
An absent reply becomes invented disinterest.
An explicit timing constraint becomes reluctance.
failure_modes.prevention: Retain evidence and mark extra interpretations hypothetical.

failure_modes.consequence: A conditional offer becomes a commitment.
failure_modes.prevention: Carry the condition into every derived output.

gosm_integration.after: Invitation components and available reply are supplied.
gosm_integration.artifact_scope: Local authored procedure, not an original skill.

content.name: Invitation follow-up choice
content.description: Select a draft acknowledgement or clarification from a response record while retaining each participant's stated boundaries.

inputs.response_record: Component-level stances with evidence and conditions.
inputs.available_actions: Concrete possible acknowledgements, clarifications or no further action.
inputs.goal: The original invitation goal, retained even when not achievable yet.

outputs.draft: A concrete unsent acknowledgement or question, or a no-action record.
outputs.reason: The explicit stance or unresolved meaning that selects it.
outputs.goal_status: Current achievable, conditional or unresolved parts.

success_criteria: An accepted bounded role is not broadened.
A stated refusal is not treated as a request for persuasion.
A condition is carried into the draft.
steps: Read the response record and its conditions.
For accepted components, draft the bounded acknowledgement.
For conditional components, expose the stated condition and an available matching option if one exists.
For unknown components, draft one question about the missing meaning when needed.
For declined components, draft an acknowledgement that leaves that component declined.
Return the draft, selection reason and remaining goal status without sending anything.
verification: Compare every proposed commitment in the draft with the supplied response record.
Confirm the original desired goal is still visible when currently unmet.
content.complexity: simple for explicit stances; moderate for mixed records.
when_to_use: A scoped response record is available and a draft next step is useful.
Several different stances occur in one reply.

examples.input: Reading accepted for two pages; hosting declined.
examples.output: Thank them for two-page reading; acknowledge no hosting; assign neither extra reading nor hosting.

examples.input: Joining conditional on audio; audio option available.
examples.output: Draft the audio option as a proposal with confirmation pending.

examples.input: Unknown whether “too much” concerns length or recurrence.
examples.output: Draft one question distinguishing those two meanings.
Acknowledge decline; do not generate persuasion as an accepted next step.

failure_modes.prevention: Retain the desired goal and its current unmet components.
Label draft and keep delivery unperformed.

failure_modes.failure: Repeated invitation after a clear no
failure_modes.prevention: Choose bounded acknowledgement or no further action.

failure_modes.failure: A promise attached to a conditional option
failure_modes.consequence: Recipient appears committed before an answer.

gosm_integration.external_gate: No external message is authorized by this artifact.

content.name: Curiosity trace record
content.description: Capture a single authored exploration step with its question, input, output, status and relation to earlier work.

inputs.question: Concrete question being explored.
inputs.source_item: Supplied text, object, construction or prior note actually used.
inputs.operation: The operation actually performed, if any.
inputs.output: Its actual text, comparison or constructed result.
inputs.prior_record: Earlier record, if a continuation exists.
inputs.interest_reason: The particular surprise or attraction; no usefulness requirement.

outputs.trace_record: Question, source, operation, output, actual/constructed/planned status, prior link, interest reason and uncertainty.
outputs.open_thread: The next unresolved question or a dead-end reason.

success_criteria: Authored results stay distinguishable from source observations.
A planned operation has no observed result attributed to it.
A dead end can retain interest without fabricated utility.
steps: Record the selected question and its interest reason.
Record the exact supplied or constructed input.
State the performed operation and preserve the resulting output.
Label whether the input/result is actual, constructed or only planned.
Link any continuation to the prior record.
Record the open question or the reason this thread stopped.
verification: Trace each claimed observation to the supplied input or actual output.
Check that the continuation refers to a record that exists.
Check that a planned test is not described as completed.
content.complexity: simple record creation with moderate status interpretation.
dependencies: An actual exploration product or explicitly planned step.
content.reuse_potential: Creative comparisons, thought experiments, interpretation exercises and later source studies.
when_to_use: A local exploration has a concrete input and output to preserve.
A proposed operation should remain visibly unperformed.

examples.input: Same question label placed at a platform and a drawing.
examples.output: Two constructed interpretations; no audience effect claimed.

examples.input: A causal experiment is proposed but not performed.
examples.output: Planned status; predicted result is a prediction.

examples.input: An explored metaphor produced no distinct comparison.
examples.output: Dead-end reason retained; interest can remain.

examples.input: A second note revises an earlier question.
examples.output: New trace linked to the earlier note and its changed question.

failure_modes.prevention: Keep interest reason separate from evidence status.

failure_modes.failure: Planned operation narrated in past tense
failure_modes.consequence: An unperformed test becomes a result.
A later question loses its derivation.
failure_modes.prevention: Carry a resolvable prior link or mark it unavailable.

failure_modes.failure: No utility is coded as no value
failure_modes.prevention: Retain the stated interest reason without promised benefit.

gosm_integration.after: Actual exploration operation or explicit plan.
gosm_integration.external_gate: Human outcome claims need observations beyond a constructed trace.

content.name: Exploration continuation choice
content.description: Choose a next local exploration operation from recorded threads using their unresolved question, distinctness, interest and resource cost.

inputs.available_interval: The present local work interval and hard dependencies.
inputs.goal: Autonomous beneficial efficient broad mind change; no forced immediate utility.

outputs.selection: One concrete next operation or a justified stopping point.
outputs.retained_threads: Other threads with their interest and reason for deferral.
outputs.expected_evidence: What the next operation can resolve and what it cannot.

success_criteria: Selected operation addresses an identified question.
Deferral does not erase a thread's interest.
A repeated result is not labeled a new benefit.
steps: Read each existing open question and stopped-thread reason.
Compare whether a proposed next operation can change a currently unresolved interpretation.
Compare local effort, hard dependencies and overlap with already recorded results.
Select a feasible operation with a distinct question; preserve pure-interest candidates even without immediate utility.
Retain the deferred threads and their reasons.
State the evidence the selected operation would provide without claiming it is already observed.
verification: Find the selected question in an existing record.
Compare the proposal with the prior output so repetition is visible.
Check that a finite constructed comparison is not represented as a human outcome.
content.complexity: moderate comparison of several live threads.
when_to_use: Several threads compete for the next local operation.
A recorded result repeats an existing distinction.

examples.input: One repeated label comparison and one new object scene.
examples.output: Select the object scene for a different referent question; retain repeated thread if still interesting.

examples.input: A test requires an unavailable participant.
examples.output: Keep the human question pending and choose an available local operation without calling it that test.

examples.input: A pure-interest thread and a direct-use thread both fit the interval.
examples.output: Compare the current question and breadth needs; pure interest remains eligible.
Stop this thread and retain its result; do not invent another pull.

failure_modes.consequence: Renaming repetition displaces a distinct question.
failure_modes.prevention: Compare the proposed operation with recorded outputs.

failure_modes.failure: Unavailable human test is replaced by fictional responses
failure_modes.consequence: The original causal question is falsely settled.
failure_modes.prevention: Keep the original test pending and state the local operation's separate scope.

failure_modes.consequence: Selected operation cannot occur in the interval.

failure_modes.prevention: Retain its open question and reason for deferral.

gosm_integration.before: A new actual local operation, or a separately available empirical study.
gosm_integration.external_gate: Human participation, time and permission remain dependencies.
gosm_integration.artifact_scope: Local selection, not autonomous control of people.
